about: Software company that developed AI-driven analytics to help legal, compliance and investigation teams review large volumes of documents and find patterns in e-discovery and data investigations. Founded in the 2010s and later acquired by Cyxtera. Customers are law firms, corporations and government agencies, paying for software and services. B2B software brand known within the legal technology niche, with no consumer profile. (Limited public information - check before outreach.)

about: Aircraft engine and systems maker based in Cincinnati, Ohio, which was the aviation division of General Electric and became GE Aerospace in 2024 when GE spun off its other businesses. It makes jet engines including the CFM LEAP (with Safran), GE9X and GEnx, plus avionics, and earns revenue from engine sales and long-term service contracts. Customers are airlines, aircraft makers and militaries. Large B2B brand with high awareness in aviation and some consumer familiarity from the GE name.

Israeli fabless chip company, SatixFy, based in Rehovot, designing satellite communication chips and digital beamforming antennas for satellite terminals, enabling flat-panel antennas for aviation, defence and mobile users. Listed on NYSE American (SATX) through a SPAC, and subject to a 2025 takeover agreement with MDA Space. Customers are satellite operators and terminal makers. B2B semiconductor brand known in the space industry, with no consumer profile.

Canadian Earth observation company, UrtheCast, based in Vancouver, that operated cameras on the International Space Station and ran a constellation plan, selling satellite imagery, video and analytics to governments, agriculture and mining customers. It struggled financially, entered creditor protection in 2020 and its assets were sold. Listed on the TSX before that. B2B space data brand with no consumer profile, and defunct in its original form.

about: Houston-based space services company, NanoRacks, which operated the first commercial space station facilities on the International Space Station, launching small satellites, running customer experiments and hosting commercial research for NASA, companies and schools. Acquired by Voyager Space in 2021. Founded in 2009. Customers are space agencies, universities and companies. B2B space services brand with a strong reputation in the industry but little general consumer recognition.

Avenger Flight Group is a Fort Lauderdale, Florida, company tagged in Crunchbase under aerospace and air transport, described as a provider of commercial aviation services. It appears to be a charter or flight services business, but the record gives no detail on its fleet, customers or scale, so confirm before outreach. (Limited public information - check before outreach.)

Swedish satellite communications company, Ovzon, based in Solna near Stockholm, operating the Ovzon 3 geostationary satellite and providing broadband connectivity for military, government and security customers worldwide, including mobile terminals. Listed on Nasdaq First North until it was acquired by Advent International in 2024. Revenue is small but growing. B2B and defence-focused brand with no consumer profile and no obvious sponsorship interest.

Atlanta software company selling workplace space management and desk booking software to corporations and universities, helping manage floor plans, moves and occupancy. Customers are facilities teams, subscribing to its cloud service. B2B software with brand awareness in workplace management only.

about: South Korean defence electronics and ICT company in the Hanwha Group, making radars, command and control systems, electro-optical sensors, communications and satellite ground equipment, along with IT services and smart city systems. Customers are the Korean armed forces, export defence buyers, and corporate clients. It is listed on the Korea Exchange and has thousands of employees. Hanwha Group is a major Korean conglomerate with significant consumer visibility through other arms like Hanwha Life and the Hanwha Eagles baseball team, though Hanwha Systems itself is mostly B2B.

US networking company that developed high-performance carrier-class routers for service providers, which was acquired by Cisco Systems in 2004 for about 89 million dollars to bolster its core routing lineup. Customers were telecom carriers and internet service providers. Defunct as an independent business. B2B with no consumer brand. It had raised substantial venture funding during the internet boom, and its engineers and technology were folded into the Cisco routing business after the deal, so the brand has not existed since.

about: US aerospace and industrial company that designs and manufactures fuel systems, engine controls, actuation, and electric power systems for aircraft and industrial engines, founded in 1870. Customers include Boeing, Airbus, GE and Caterpillar, and the business makes tens of thousands of products, with annual sales of about three billion dollars. Headquartered in Colorado, it is listed on Nasdaq (WWD). B2B component supplier with little consumer visibility, although the name is known in aviation engineering.

about: Belgium-based provider of airport ground support equipment and services, supplying baggage tractors, loaders, ground power and other vehicles to airlines and handlers via leasing and maintenance. It serves airports across Europe, the Middle East, North America and Asia, and has a fleet of tens of thousands of units. TCR is privately owned. B2B airport services supplier with no consumer profile, but widely seen on airport aprons.

US space company that provided launch services for small satellites through the SpaceX rideshare, and later spun off its Earth imaging business as BlackSky. Customers were satellite manufacturers and governments. It was headquartered in Seattle and venture-backed. The company's later activities were reorganised into BlackSky, listed in 2021. B2B space business with minimal public profile. The company later became the main owner of the BlackSky satellite imagery business, which listed on the NYSE in 2021, and its brand has largely disappeared.

US drone company that makes professional drones and software for mapping, surveying and inspection, including the Solo and Site Scan products. It was co-founded by Chris Anderson and Jordi Munoz, and raised about 100 million dollars from backers such as Atmel and Foundry Group, then shifted from consumer drones to software, working with Autodesk. B2B and prosumer, with decent awareness in the drone community.

Austrian technology company that develops safe networked computing platforms for aerospace, automotive and industrial markets, with time-triggered Ethernet networks, flight control systems and advanced driver assistance technology. Customers are aircraft makers such as Boeing and Airbus, carmakers and industrial firms, and revenue comes from hardware, software and licensing. Founded in 1998 in Vienna with investors including Audi, Infineon and Samsung. B2B supplier with no consumer brand.

US engineering and information technology staffing company in Philadelphia that provided contract staffing, engineering and technical services to industrial, aerospace and energy customers, with offices in the US, UK, Canada and the Middle East. Revenue was well over a billion dollars at its peak. It was listed on the NYSE (CDI) and acquired by AE Industrial Partners in 2017, after which it was privately held. B2B staffing business with a well-known name in engineering recruitment, but no consumer profile.

US air cargo and aircraft leasing group, Air Transport Services Group (ATSG), that leases freighter aircraft and provides air cargo transportation, maintenance and ground services, including to Amazon and DHL, through airlines such as ABX Air, Air Transport International and Omni Air. It owns and leases around 100 or more aircraft. Listed on Nasdaq (ATSG). In 2025 it was taken private by Stonepeak. B2B logistics business with little consumer awareness.

Chinese information-technology company with activities linked to aerospace and mobile enterprise software, apparently providing software and systems services to large organisations. The headquarters listed and the specific products and customers cannot be confirmed from the information available. (Limited public information - check before outreach.)

Adam Aircraft Industries was a Colorado aircraft maker that developed the A500 twin-engine piston aircraft and the A700 AdamJet very light jet, using composite construction. Founded in 2000 by Rick Adam, it delivered a small number of A500 aircraft to private owners and air-taxi operators but ran short of capital and filed for bankruptcy in 2008; its assets were bought by Triton Aerospace. Customers were private buyers and business-aviation operators. Defunct brand, B2B and high-net-worth niche; no active sponsorship relevance.

about: Digifi Korea, as referenced by Crunchbase, is a South Korean satellite communications and information technology company based in Seoul, providing maritime and remote-area connectivity services. Customers are shipping fleets, energy companies and enterprises needing satellite broadband, paying subscription and equipment fees. Private firm, B2B focus. Little consumer brand awareness; any sponsorship appeal would lie in shipping and offshore industry networks.

Killick Aerospace is a Dallas-based aviation company supplying commercial engine and aircraft parts and offering aircraft and engine leasing, trading and professional aerospace services. Its customers are airlines, lessors and maintenance providers worldwide, and it earns from parts sales, lease income and service fees. Privately held and mid-sized. Pure B2B aerospace supplier with no consumer profile, though it is known within aircraft-trading circles.

about: Northstar Aerospace was a Canadian-listed (TSX) maker of helicopter and aircraft transmission components, gears and drive systems, with plants in Milton, Ontario, Bedford Park, Illinois and in the UK. B2B only, with no consumer awareness and no current sponsorship relevance.

about: XO is a private aviation company based in Fort Lauderdale offering jet charter, jet cards and membership on a marketplace of operators, plus a fleet of its own Citation jets, to wealthy individuals and corporate flyers. Founded in 2009 as XOJET, it bought Vistajet's US business in 2016 and was acquired by Vista Global in 2020, becoming part of the Vista group. Its customers are US-based, flying thousands of destinations. Recognisable luxury aviation brand with sports and event partnerships.

about: Mesa Air Group is a Phoenix-based regional airline holding company listed on Nasdaq (MESA) that flies capacity-purchase agreement flights as American Eagle, United Express and previously US Airways Express, operating regional jets between hub airports and smaller cities across North America. Founded in 1982, it carries millions of passengers a year but its brand is hidden behind the partner airlines. Revenue is paid per block hour by the airlines. Low consumer awareness for the Mesa name.

Autonomous Control Systems Laboratory (ACSL) is a Tokyo-based Japanese drone maker, listed on the Tokyo Stock Exchange (6232), founded as a spin-off from Chiba University. It develops industrial drones and flight control software for inspection, logistics, surveying and security, including its SOTEN model, with customers among Japanese utilities, government and companies. Revenue is a few billion yen. B2B drone specialist known within Japan's drone industry and with limited consumer awareness.

Avanti Communications was a London satellite operator that provided Ka-band broadband capacity across Europe, the Middle East and Africa using its HYLAS satellites, selling to telecom operators, governments, broadcasters and enterprises. It was listed on AIM and the LSE, then restructured its heavy debt in 2017, with creditors taking control and the shares delisted. It continues as a private satellite broadband provider. B2B infrastructure brand with no consumer awareness.

Heroux-Devtek is a Longueuil, Quebec maker of aircraft landing gear and aerostructures, supplying fighter, transport and commercial aircraft programmes and servicing the Lockheed Martin F-35, Boeing and Airbus platforms, with plants across Canada, the US, the UK and Spain. It was listed on the TSX (HRX) until acquired by Platinum Equity in a deal worth around 1.4 billion Canadian dollars. B2B aerospace supplier with no consumer brand.

Bermuda-based satellite operator that bought and launched the ProtoStar I geostationary satellite to lease capacity to broadcasters and data customers in Asia. Founded in 2005, raised money from investors including Protostar's private equity backers, but could not sustain the debt, and filed for bankruptcy in 2009 with assets sold to Intelsat. Defunct. No consumer brand. The satellite was launched in 2009 on a Proton rocket, and the company lasted only a few years.

about: Wheels Up is a US private aviation company offering jet card memberships, charter flights, fractional-style access and aircraft management using its own and partner fleets of light, midsize and large jets. Customers are corporates and wealthy individuals. Headquartered in New York; founded 2013. Listed on the New York Stock Exchange (UP) via a 2021 SPAC merger, with Delta Air Lines as a major shareholder, and had a rescue financing in 2024. Known in the private flying market, with sports and events partnerships.

Hainan Airlines is a Chinese full-service airline founded in 1993 and based on Hainan island, a subsidiary of HNA group, now flagship of Hainan Airlines Holding under a 2021 restructuring led by Liaoning Fangda. Flies domestic and international routes from Haikou, Beijing and elsewhere, serving leisure and business travellers. Listed on the Shanghai Stock Exchange (600221). Well-known Chinese carrier with a Skytrax five-star rating history.

about: Alaska Airlines is a major US carrier, the fifth largest after merging Hawaiian Airlines in 2024, flying passengers and cargo from hubs in Seattle, Portland, Anchorage, Los Angeles, San Francisco and Honolulu. Operates a fleet of Boeing 737s plus regional partners, with revenue near 14 billion dollars. Headquartered in Seattle (SeaTac), founded 1932. Subsidiary of Alaska Air Group, listed on the New York Stock Exchange (ALK). Strong West Coast consumer brand, with college and pro sports partnerships.

American Airlines is the world's largest airline by fleet size and passengers, flying to over 350 destinations from hubs in Dallas-Fort Worth, Charlotte, Chicago, Miami, Philadelphia and Phoenix, and a member of Oneworld. Revenue near 54 billion dollars, with about 130,000 employees. Headquartered in Fort Worth, Texas; formed 1930. Listed on Nasdaq (AAL). Has restructured after the 2013 US Airways merger. Household US consumer brand with long-standing sports naming rights (American Airlines Center and Arena).

Southwest Airlines is a US low-cost carrier, the largest domestic carrier by passengers, flying a Boeing 737 fleet to more than 100 destinations, historically with open seating and free checked bags (changed in 2025). Revenue near 28 billion dollars. Headquartered in Dallas, Texas; founded 1967. Listed on the New York Stock Exchange (LUV). Activist investor Elliott pressed changes in 2024. Well known US consumer brand with extensive sports partnerships.

United Airlines is one of the largest US carriers, flying passengers and cargo to more than 300 destinations from hubs in Chicago, Newark, Houston, Denver, San Francisco, Los Angeles and Washington, as a Star Alliance member with the MileagePlus loyalty programme. Revenue near 57 billion dollars and about 100,000 employees. Headquartered in Chicago; part of United Airlines Holdings, listed on Nasdaq (UAL). Major US consumer brand with extensive sports and entertainment sponsorships.

International Airlines Group (IAG) is the parent of British Airways, Iberia, Vueling, Aer Lingus, Level and the loyalty scheme Avios, flying to more than 200 destinations and carrying over 100 million passengers a year. Revenue near 33 billion euros. Headquartered in London (with Madrid origins), formed 2011. Listed in London and Madrid (IAG). Strong airline brands with substantial sponsorships, such as British Airways' links to sport.

NEOM is a Saudi Arabian giga-project in the northwest of the country, owned by the Public Investment Fund and headed from Riyadh. It is planned as a set of new developments including The Line linear city, Oxagon industrial port, Trojena mountain resort (host of the 2029 Asian Winter Games), Sindalah island and the Magna region, with a focus on tourism, green hydrogen, real estate and technology. Funding comes from the PIF and bonds, with spending in the tens of billions of dollars. Government-backed. NEOM is a prominent sponsor, with partnerships in football, sailing, McLaren's Extreme E and other global sport.

Sumisho Air Lease is an aircraft leasing company, a subsidiary of Japan's Sumitomo Corporation, with a US office in Los Angeles. It buys commercial aircraft and engines and leases them to airlines, earning rental income and sale gains, and was later merged into the Sumitomo group aviation leasing platform. Funding of about $19bn in the input appears to be a debt or facility figure and may be garbled by OCR. B2B lessor with no consumer profile, and a poor sponsorship target.

about: Surf Air Mobility is a Los Angeles regional air mobility company, owning Surf Air membership flights, commuter airline Southern Airways Express and the electric aircraft powertrain developer Surf Air Mobility electrification unit. It offers subscription and per-flight travel between regional airports, mostly in the US, using Cessna Caravan aircraft. Listed on the NYSE (SRFM) since 2023, after raising about $825m. Niche consumer brand with moderate profile among frequent regional flyers and a premium customer base.

AerCap is the world's largest aircraft lessor, headquartered in Dublin, with owned and managed assets of aircraft, engines and helicopters worth tens of billions of dollars. It leases planes to about 300 airlines worldwide, earning rental income and sale gains, and completed its purchase of GE Capital Aviation Services in 2021. Listed on the NYSE (AER) and led by Aengus Kelly. B2B financier, known in aviation, with no consumer awareness.

LATAM Airlines Group is Latin America's largest airline group, headquartered in Santiago, Chile, with affiliates in Brazil, Peru, Colombia, Ecuador and Argentina, flying to over 140 destinations plus a cargo arm. It carries over 70 million passengers a year, with annual revenue near $13bn, and emerged from US Chapter 11 in 2022. Listed on the Santiago stock exchange (LTM) and NYSE ADRs. Strong regional consumer brand with sponsorship in sports across Latin America and international football.

VietJet Air is a Vietnamese low-cost airline founded by Nguyen Thi Phuong Thao, based in Ho Chi Minh City and Hanoi, flying domestic and international routes across Asia and beyond with an Airbus A320 family and A330 fleet and a large Boeing 737 MAX order. It carries tens of millions of passengers a year. Listed on the Ho Chi Minh Stock Exchange (VJC). Strong consumer brand in Vietnam, known for flamboyant marketing, and an active sports sponsor.

DSV is a Danish global transport and logistics company, headquartered in Hedehusene, near Copenhagen, offering air and sea freight, road transport and contract logistics in about 80 countries. After buying DB Schenker in 2025 for about DKK 106bn, it has more than 150,000 employees, with revenue above DKK 200bn. Listed on Nasdaq Copenhagen (DSV). B2B logistics firm with strong industry reputation, and its trucks and containers carry the brand, but consumers rarely know it.

Heathrow Airport Holdings owns and operates London Heathrow, Britain's busiest airport and one of the world's largest hubs, handling about 83 million passengers a year across four terminals. It earns aeronautical charges from airlines and retail, parking and property revenue. Owned by a consortium led by Ferrovial, Qatar Investment Authority, Canada's CDPQ and GIC, Alinda, USS and others, with Ferrovial reducing its stake. Private. Hugely recognised consumer-facing brand, with premium sponsorship opportunities.

Vietnam Airlines is Vietnam's state-owned flag carrier, based in Hanoi, with a fleet of Airbus and Boeing aircraft (including A350 and 787) flying to over 20 countries and many domestic routes under the Golden Lotus brand, and a member of SkyTeam. It carries over 20 million passengers a year, with Vietnam Airlines Group also owning Pacific Airlines and VASCO. Majority-owned by the government through SCIC and listed on the Vietnamese UPCoM market (HVN). Strongly recognised by Vietnamese consumers, with sports and event sponsorships.

Bangalore International Airport Limited (BIAL) operates Kempegowda International Airport in Bengaluru, India's third busiest airport, handling over 40 million passengers a year, with a new Terminal 2. It earns airline charges, retail, advertising and property income. Owned by the GVK Group's successor Fairfax, Fairfax India Holdings (about 64 percent), with Siemens-related and Karnataka government stakes. Private. Consumer-facing airport brand in a major city, with sponsorship and advertising inventory.

gategroup is a Swiss airline catering and onboard services company, based in Glattbrugg near Zurich, supplying meals, retail products, equipment and lounges to airlines worldwide through more than 190 units in about 60 countries. It was acquired by RRJ Capital in 2016 and later had HNA and Temasek links, restructured and sold to new owners. Private. B2B with little consumer brand recognition, though its products are used on airlines passengers' flights.

Gol Linhas Aereas (Gol Transportes Aereos) is a Brazilian low-cost airline based in Sao Paulo, flying a Boeing 737 fleet on domestic and South American routes, with more than 30 million passengers a year. It filed for US Chapter 11 in January 2024 and emerged in June 2025 with Abra Group as its parent, after which it delisted from the NYSE and B3. Revenue is near BRL 20bn. Well-known Brazilian consumer airline brand, with football and sports sponsorship history.

Virgin Atlantic Airways is a British long-haul airline based in Crawley, West Sussex, flying from London Heathrow, Gatwick and Manchester to North America, the Caribbean, Africa, India and Asia, with about 40 aircraft and over 5 million passengers a year. Delta Air Lines holds 49 percent, Virgin Group 51 percent, and the airline is private. It emerged from a 2020 rescue package. Strong consumer brand with the Virgin name, and sponsorship and brand tie-ins.

Grupo Aeromexico is Mexico's flag-carrier airline group based in Mexico City, flying domestic and international routes to the US, Latin America, Europe and Asia from its Mexico City hub, and a founding member of the SkyTeam alliance. It carries about 25 million passengers a year, with a fleet of roughly 150 aircraft. Delta Air Lines owns a stake of around 20 percent. It returned to the Mexican exchange and the NYSE in 2025 (AEROMEX). High consumer brand awareness in Mexico.

JetBlue Airways is a New York (Long Island City) passenger airline founded in 1998 that flies from hubs at New York JFK, Boston and Fort Lauderdale to destinations in the US, Caribbean, Latin America and Europe, with a fleet of about 280 aircraft and annual revenue near $9 billion. Listed on Nasdaq (JBLU). Customers are leisure and business travellers. High consumer brand awareness in the US, a sponsor of sports teams including the Boston Red Sox and Fenway Park.

Delta Air Lines is a major US airline headquartered in Atlanta, Georgia and listed on the NYSE (DAL). It operates a hub-and-spoke network to over 275 destinations on six continents, carrying over 200 million passengers a year with a fleet of roughly 1,000 aircraft and revenue of about 60 billion dollars. It also has a loyalty programme (SkyMiles), cargo and MRO services, and owns a refinery. Founded 1925. Very strong consumer brand, SkyTeam founding member, and an active sports marketer.

Garuda Indonesia is the national flag carrier airline of Indonesia, headquartered at Jakarta, majority owned by the Indonesian government and listed on the Indonesia Stock Exchange. It operates domestic and international flights from Jakarta and Bali with a fleet of Boeing and Airbus jets, plus subsidiary Citilink as a low-cost carrier. Founded 1949. It restructured about 9 billion dollars of debt in 2022. Strong national consumer brand and SkyTeam member.

Ryanair is Europe's largest low-cost airline group by passengers, headquartered in Dublin and listed on Euronext Dublin and Nasdaq (RYAAY). It flies a fleet of about 600 Boeing 737s to over 230 airports in 37 countries, carrying more than 200 million passengers a year with revenue near 14 billion euros. Group airlines include Buzz, Malta Air and Lauda Europe. Founded 1984 and led by Michael O'Leary. Very high consumer recognition, known for aggressive, humorous advertising.

Azerbaijan Airlines (AZAL) is the national flag carrier of Azerbaijan, headquartered in Baku and owned by the state. It flies Airbus, Boeing and Embraer aircraft to destinations in Europe, Asia and the Middle East, and is the main carrier at Baku's Heydar Aliyev airport. Founded in 1992 from the Soviet-era Aeroflot division. One of its aircraft crashed near Aktau, Kazakhstan, in December 2024. Established national brand in a country that hosts an F1 race at Baku.

Spirit Airlines is a US ultra-low-cost carrier, historically headquartered in Miramar, Florida and now shown near Dania Beach, with a fleet of Airbus A320 family aircraft flying across the US, Caribbean and Latin America under a bare-fare, pay-for-extras model. It failed to merge with Frontier or JetBlue, filed for chapter 11 bankruptcy in November 2024 and again in 2025, and has been shrinking. Founded 1983. Recognisable consumer brand, but financially distressed, so a weak sponsorship prospect.

Fraport Greece operates, manages and develops 14 regional airports in Greece, including Thessaloniki, Mykonos, Santorini, Corfu, Rhodes and Chania, under a 40-year concession from 2017, owned by Germany's Fraport AG and the Greek Copelouzos Group. Headquartered in Athens, it earns airport charges, retail and parking from airlines and over 35 million annual passengers, and invests in terminals. Customers are airlines and travellers. B2B airport operator with tourism-driven visibility across Greek islands.

Mundys, formerly Atlantia, is an Italian infrastructure group headquartered in Rome that owns and operates toll roads and airports, including Abertis, Aeroports de Paris stake, Telepass and Aeroporti di Roma. It is controlled by the Benetton family's Edizione and, since 2022, partly owned by Blackstone Infrastructure. Revenue is about 8 billion euros. Customers are motorists, airlines and airport passengers, with a footprint across Europe and the Americas. Telepass is a visible consumer brand in Italy; the group otherwise is B2B.

ixigo (Le Travenues Technology) is an Indian online travel platform and app for train, flight, bus and hotel bookings, particularly strong in rail ticketing with live train status and tools, aimed at mass-market travellers. Based in Gurugram, founded in 2007. Revenue comes from commissions and advertising. Listed on the NSE and BSE since its 2024 IPO. Crunchbase shows about $339 million in funding. Widely used consumer app in India.

Italian flag carrier airline based at Rome Fiumicino, created in 2021 as successor to Alitalia and owned by the Italian Treasury with Lufthansa Group taking a minority stake in 2025. Flies about 80 aircraft to Europe, the Americas and Asia. Strong Italian consumer brand with sports sponsorship, including the Italian national team. ITA has a fleet of about 90 aircraft and over 5,000 employees, and has been backed by the Italian Treasury.

New Saudi flag carrier based in Riyadh, owned by the Public Investment Fund and launched in 2023, with orders for Boeing 787 and Airbus A321neo aircraft and first commercial flights in 2025-26. Targets premium international travellers. New consumer brand with sports sponsorship, including the shirt of Atletico Madrid. The airline plans to operate from King Salman International Airport and has booked aircraft from Boeing and Airbus.

Mumbai-based airport operator of Chhatrapati Shivaji Maharaj International Airport, majority-owned by Adani Airport Holdings with Airports Authority of India. Customers are airlines and passengers, earning aeronautical and retail revenue. Strong regional brand, with large passenger traffic. Handles tens of millions of passengers each year. Operated by a public-private partnership in which Adani Group holds the majority. Brand is regional. The airport operates two terminals and handles about 50 million passengers annually.

Shanghai-based flag carrier airline, one of China's big three, flying domestic and international routes, member of SkyTeam, state-owned and listed in Shanghai, Hong Kong and NYSE. Revenue about CNY 140 billion. Strong consumer brand in China. Part of China Eastern Air Holdings, with a fleet of over 700 aircraft. Hub airports in Shanghai Pudong and Hongqiao. Strong consumer brand across China.

HALO AirFinance is a joint venture between Tokyo Century and Carlyle Aviation Partners, based in Fort Lauderdale, Florida, formed to provide aircraft finance, specifically financing for commercial airlines and lessors. Customers are airlines and aircraft owners. Funding of about 390 million dollars is shown. B2B financial services business with no consumer brand awareness, though both parents are well known in finance and aviation.

about: Reliable Robotics is a Mountain View aviation technology company developing automated flight systems that let cargo aircraft such as the Cessna 208 Caravan fly with remote pilots on the ground. The company works with the FAA and the US Air Force and has partnered with cargo operators, including regional cargo carriers. Founded in 2017, it has raised about 410 million dollars from investors including Eclipse and Lightspeed. B2B aviation technology with some visibility in the aerospace sector.

Ethiopian Airlines is Ethiopia's state-owned flag carrier and Africa's largest airline by fleet and revenue, headquartered in Addis Ababa with a hub at Bole International Airport, flying to over 140 destinations worldwide. It is a Star Alliance member and operates Boeing and Airbus fleets, with cargo, MRO and training businesses. Funding shown is about 1.1 billion dollars. Strong brand across Africa, and sponsors of sport and events.

Virgin Australia is Australia's second-largest airline, headquartered in Brisbane, flying domestic and some international routes with a leisure and business offer and the Velocity Frequent Flyer programme. It entered administration in 2020 and was bought by US private equity firm Bain Capital, relaunching as a mid-market carrier. Bain Capital reintroduced it to the ASX in 2025, with Qatar Airways taking a minority stake. Revenue is over 5 billion Australian dollars. High consumer awareness in Australia, and has sponsored motorsport and other sport in the past.

Aegean Airlines is Greece's largest airline, based in Kifisia near Athens, flying scheduled and charter routes across Europe and the Mediterranean, and a Star Alliance member since 2010. It acquired Olympic Air in 2013 and operates a fleet of Airbus aircraft. Listed on the Athens Stock Exchange (AEGN), with revenue of over 1.5 billion euros and about 15 million passengers a year. Very high consumer visibility in Greece, with a history of sports sponsorship.

Beond is a Dubai-based premium leisure airline, founded in the Maldives and Dubai, which flies business-class style services between Europe, the Middle East and the Maldives using Airbus A319 aircraft with 44 seats. It aims at high-end holidaymakers and sells tickets directly. Total funding is about $155 million, and it launched flights in 2022. It is a niche, small brand with limited awareness outside luxury travel and the Maldives market.

Willis Mitsui & Co. Engine Support is a Dublin-based aircraft engine leasing joint venture between Willis Lease Finance and Mitsui & Co., providing aircraft engines to airlines worldwide on lease. Recorded funding is about $750 million. Customers are airlines and maintenance firms. B2B with low public brand awareness.

Finnair is Finland's flag-carrier airline, headquartered in Helsinki and listed on Nasdaq Helsinki (FIA), flying to Europe and Asia via its Helsinki hub, with about 14 million passengers a year and a fleet of Airbus aircraft. The Finnish government owns about 55 percent. It is a strong consumer brand in the Nordics and a member of the oneworld alliance.

Malaysian low-cost airline brand founded in 2001 by Tony Fernandes, now under the Capital A group, flying across Asia with about 200 aircraft. Large following, sponsor of football and motorsport. Tony Fernandes and Kamarudin Meranun bought the airline in 2001 for a token sum. Fernandes also ran the Caterham Formula 1 team and the airline sponsored F1 outfits in that period. The AirAsia group, now Capital A, also has the AirAsia Move super-app. Strong consumer brand across Southeast Asia.

Kuwaiti low-cost airline operating scheduled flights from Kuwait to the Middle East, Asia and Europe with Airbus A320 and A220 aircraft. Listed on Boursa Kuwait. Founder Marwan Boodai started it as Kuwait's first private airline in 2004, listing on the Kuwait exchange in 2005. It operates from Terminal 5 at Kuwait International Airport, and also runs Jazeera Terminal Services for ground handling. Strong regional brand awareness.

Chicago-based producer of sustainable aviation fuel, using proprietary ethanol-to-jet technology licensed to producers and now running its own Freedom Pines plant in Georgia. Customers are airlines and fuel buyers. Backed by Microsoft, Shell, Suncor and British Airways. B2B energy technology company with limited consumer awareness but notable airline partnerships.

Operator of Strickland Brothers 10 Minute Oil Change service centres, a US automotive chain offering quick oil changes, tyre services and related maintenance for everyday motorists. Customers are drivers who stay in their cars while service is done. Franchised and company-run locations. Regional consumer brand with local rather than national awareness.

about: Hong Kong's flagship airline, Cathay Pacific, flying to over 80 destinations with a hub at Hong Kong International Airport. Owned by Swire, Air China and Qatar Airways; listed on HKEX (293). Cathay was founded in 1946, and Swire holds roughly 45 percent. It also runs HK Express, bought in 2019, and cargo airline Air Hong Kong. It sponsors the Hong Kong Sevens. High-visibility consumer brand and prior sports sponsor including rugby sevens.

Chinese aircraft developer engaged in research and development of aviation vehicles, according to the input, in air transportation and industrial technology. Customers would be airlines and industrial buyers. B2B development company with limited public awareness; scale and funding are not confirmed here.
cb_desc: Zero Gravity Aircraft Industry is engaged in the R&D and....

about: Sichuan Airlines is a Chinese airline based in Chengdu, operating an all-Airbus fleet of more than 150 aircraft on domestic and international routes, with Chengdu Tianfu and Shuangliu airports as key hubs. It was founded in 1986 and its shareholders include Sichuan Airlines Group, Shandong Airlines Group and other state-linked entities. It is known for its Tibetan routes and for the 2018 cockpit window incident. It is a well known Chinese consumer airline brand, with annual passenger numbers in the tens of millions.

Infratil is a New Zealand infrastructure investment company based in Wellington, managed by Morrison & Co. Its holdings include CDC Data Centres in Australia, Manawa Energy, Longroad Energy, Qscan and Wellington Airport stake. It is listed on the NZX and ASX (IFT) and is among the largest NZX companies. Infratil invests across digital infrastructure, renewable energy, healthcare and airports. It is a financial investor with strong recognition among NZ investors, but low consumer brand awareness itself.

AS Mileage Plan is the entity linked to the Alaska Airlines Mileage Plan loyalty programme, used in a financing structure by Alaska Air Group, the US airline parent of Alaska Airlines. Crunchbase lists about $500 million of funding, most likely a loan secured by the loyalty program. The input does not give a headquarters. It is a financing vehicle rather than an operating brand, but the Mileage Plan itself is well known to US air travelers. (Limited public information - check before outreach.)
cb_desc: AS Mileage Plan IP is a airline based entity.

about: FLYR is a San Francisco technology company using AI to provide revenue management, pricing and passenger service systems for airlines, including its Revenue Operating System and Pros-like offerings, with customers such as Avelo and Riyadh Air-linked partners. It acquired Hospitality Solutions (Pace) and Batch in 2022-2023 and later the Radixx business, and has raised close to $480 million. Founded in 2013 by Alex Mans, it is B2B, mostly known among airlines.
cb_desc: FLYR is a technology company that uses Al to help airlines an...

about: Philippine Airlines is the flag carrier of the Philippines and Asia's oldest commercial airline, founded in 1941 and based in Pasay City, Metro Manila. It flies domestic routes and international services across Asia, the Middle East, North America, Europe and Australia, with a fleet of Airbus and Boeing aircraft, and is controlled by the Lucio Tan Group. It carries over 10 million passengers a year in good years. It is a major consumer brand in the Philippines and among Filipino diaspora travelers.

Turkish Airlines is the Turkish national flag carrier, based in Istanbul, flying to more than 340 destinations in over 130 countries, which is among the largest networks in the world. It operates a large fleet of Airbus and Boeing aircraft, from the new Istanbul Airport hub, and has around 85 million passengers a year plus a big cargo arm. It is listed on Borsa Istanbul (THYAO) and majority held by the Turkey Wealth Fund. It is a major consumer brand and sponsors football and basketball clubs.

Air Europa is a Spanish airline based in the Balearic Islands (Llucmajor, Mallorca) with its main hub in Madrid, flying domestic and international routes to Europe, North and South America and the Caribbean with Boeing 787s and 737s. It belongs to the Globalia group. In 2024-2025 Turkish Airlines took a minority stake after IAG's planned takeover was dropped. It is a SkyTeam member and is a widely recognized airline brand in Spain and Latin America.

Breeze Airways is a US low-fare airline founded by JetBlue founder David Neeleman, with headquarters in Cottonwood Heights near Salt Lake City, Utah. It began flying in 2021 and operates Airbus A220 and Embraer jets on point-to-point routes between underserved cities in the US and the Caribbean, with a fare structure branded Nice, Nicer and Nicest. It has raised around $335 million from private investors. It is a growing consumer airline brand with regional awareness.

flynas is a Saudi low-cost airline based in Riyadh, founded in 2007 as Nas Air, flying domestic and international routes from Riyadh, Jeddah and Dammam to the Middle East, Europe, Asia and Africa. It operates a fleet of Airbus A320 family aircraft and has ordered many more A320neo and A330neo jets. It listed on the Saudi Exchange (Tadawul) in 2025. It carries over 15 million passengers a year and is a well known consumer airline brand in Saudi Arabia.

T'way Air is a South Korean low-cost airline based in Seoul that operates domestic and international flights, mostly to Japan, Southeast Asia, China and in 2023 onwards Europe after taking over Eurasian routes from Korean Air's Asiana merger. It started in 2005 as Hansung Airlines and is listed on KOSDAQ (091810). Consumer brand with solid awareness in Korea.

Akasa Air is an Indian low-cost airline based in Mumbai, launched in August 2022 and backed by the late investor Rakesh Jhunjhunwala, flying domestic routes and some Gulf destinations with Boeing 737 MAX aircraft. It competes with IndiGo and Air India for budget travellers. Operated by SNV Aviation, it has grown quickly to a fleet of dozens of jets. Consumer airline brand with fast-growing awareness in India.

EasyJet is a British low-cost airline founded in 1995 by Stelios Haji-Ioannou and headquartered at London Luton Airport. It operates a fleet of around 350 Airbus A320 family aircraft to over 150 airports in more than 35 countries, carrying roughly 90 million passengers a year, and sells package holidays via easyJet holidays. Revenue is about 9 billion pounds. Listed on the London Stock Exchange (EZJ) and FTSE 100 member. A well-known European consumer brand with high retail awareness.

China Southern Airlines is one of China's three largest state-owned airlines, headquartered in Guangzhou, with a fleet of around 900 aircraft serving more than 200 destinations. It flies from hubs in Guangzhou and Beijing Daxing, and is a member of the SkyTeam alliance. Revenue is above 20 billion dollars and it carries more than 100 million passengers a year. Controlled by China Southern Air Holding, a state-owned enterprise, and listed in Shanghai (600029), Hong Kong (1055) and NYSE (ZNH). Strong consumer brand in China and Asia.

Wizz Air is a Hungarian ultra-low-cost airline, founded in 2003 and headquartered in Budapest, with a fleet of roughly 200 Airbus A320 family aircraft flying to more than 190 destinations across Europe, the Middle East and Central Asia, carrying about 60 million passengers a year. It is listed on the London Stock Exchange (WIZZ), and was Europe's biggest budget carrier in Central and Eastern Europe. Revenue is around 5 billion euros. High consumer brand visibility in Europe; has sponsored football clubs and events.

The Office National Des Aeroports (ONDA) is Morocco's national airports authority, a state-owned body managing 19 or more civil airports, including Casablanca Mohammed V, Marrakech, Agadir and Rabat, and air navigation and training services. Headquartered in Casablanca, it handles tens of millions of passengers a year and is investing in expansion for the 2030 World Cup. Government-owned B2B and public infrastructure, with high visibility to travellers in Morocco.

Saudi Ground Services Company (SGS) is the Saudi Arabian ground handling provider, offering aircraft handling, cargo, passenger services and fuel and catering support at airports across the Kingdom, including Jeddah, Riyadh and Dammam. It is a subsidiary of Saudia Group and is listed on the Saudi Exchange (Tadawul 4031). Headquartered in Jeddah. Funding is shown in riyals (about 850 million). B2B aviation services, with no consumer brand though tied to Saudia.

Avelo Airlines is a US low-cost airline based in Houston that launched in 2021, flying Boeing 737s and then Embraer jets from secondary airports such as Burbank, New Haven and Wilmington to leisure destinations in Florida, the Northeast and the West. It also operates deportation flights for the US government under contract. Founded by Andrew Levy, it is privately held with about $175 million raised. Moderate consumer brand awareness in its regional markets.

XCF Global is a Houston company producing sustainable aviation fuel, through its renewable diesel and SAF facility in Reno, Nevada, with other projects planned. It merged with a SPAC in 2025 and is listed on Nasdaq (SAFX). Customers are airlines and fuel distributors. Early stage with about 30 million dollars of funding and low consumer brand awareness. The company is early stage, with no meaningful sales yet, and depends on financing for its plans. It has no consumer brand, though sustainable aviation fuel is a topical area.

AGS Airports is the owner and operator of Aberdeen, Glasgow and Southampton airports in the UK, headquartered in Paisley, Scotland. Together the three airports handle over 15 million passengers a year, earning revenue from airline passenger charges, retail, parking and property. It was long owned by Ferrovial and Macquarie-managed funds. Glasgow is the largest, with routes to Europe and North America, while Aberdeen serves the North Sea energy sector. B2B infrastructure operator whose airport brands are well known to UK travellers.

Cebu Pacific, operated by Cebu Air Inc. and listed on the Philippine Stock Exchange (CEB), is the Philippines' largest low-cost carrier, based in Pasay City and founded in 1988 by the Gokongwei family's JG Summit group. It flies domestic and international routes across Asia, Australia and the Middle East with a fleet of about 90 Airbus aircraft, and carries over 20 million passengers a year. Revenue comes from fares and ancillaries. Very high consumer visibility in the Philippines.

Royal Jordanian Airlines is the flag carrier of Jordan, based in Amman, and founded in 1963 as Alia. It flies from its Queen Alia International Airport hub to over 40 destinations in the Middle East, Europe, Asia and North America. It has been a member of the oneworld alliance since 2007, and carries around 3 million passengers a year with a fleet of Airbus and Embraer aircraft. The Jordanian government remains the majority owner. Strong brand in Jordan and the region and an established sponsor of local events.

El Al Israel Airlines is the flag carrier of Israel, based in Tel Aviv at Ben Gurion Airport and listed on the Tel Aviv Stock Exchange. It flies passengers and cargo to destinations in Europe, North America and Asia with a fleet of Boeing aircraft, and also operates the Sundor and Up brands. It was founded in 1948 and privatised in 2004, and carries around 6-7 million passengers a year. Strong, widely recognised national brand and a sponsor of cultural and sporting events in Israel.

Scandinavian Airlines (SAS) is the flag carrier of Denmark, Norway and Sweden, based in Solna near Stockholm, and a member of the SkyTeam alliance. It flies to over 100 destinations from hubs in Copenhagen, Oslo and Stockholm, carrying about 25-30 million passengers a year. It restructured through Chapter 11 in the US in 2022-2024, and in 2025 Air France-KLM agreed to take a majority stake. Strong consumer brand in Scandinavia and a sponsor of sporting and cultural events.

Malaysia Airlines is Malaysia's flag carrier, based at Kuala Lumpur International Airport in Sepang, Selangor, and part of Malaysia Aviation Group. It is a member of the oneworld alliance and flies to about 60 destinations across Asia, Europe, Australia and the Middle East. It is owned by the government through Khazanah Nasional, after being restructured following the 2014 flight disappearances, and carries around 15-20 million passengers a year. Strong national consumer brand and a visible sponsor of sporting and cultural events in Malaysia.

Gogo is an inflight internet and connectivity provider for business aviation, listed on Nasdaq (GOGO) and based in the US (Broomfield, Colorado, with a headquarters in McLean, Virginia in the listing). It sells Wi-Fi equipment and services to business jet owners and operators, and sold its commercial airline business to Intelsat in 2020. Its networks include air-to-ground and satellite service, and it serves thousands of aircraft. Revenue is around $400 million. B2B brand, known to aviation customers and travellers through airline Wi-Fi logos in the past.

Aireon is a McLean, Virginia company that provides global space-based air traffic surveillance, using ADS-B receivers hosted on Iridium NEXT satellites to track aircraft in real time, including over oceans and remote regions. Customers are air navigation service providers such as NAV CANADA, NATS and the FAA, and airlines, who pay for data services. It was founded in 2011 and is owned by Iridium and a group of air navigation service providers, with about $339 million raised. B2B aviation technology brand with no consumer awareness.

Operator of Florence (Amerigo Vespucci) and Pisa (Galileo Galilei) airports in Tuscany, Italy, managing passenger services, retail and cargo. Pisa is the region's main airport for low-cost and leisure traffic and Florence serves business and short-haul routes, with income from airline charges, shops and parking. Controlled by Corporacion America Italia. Listed historically on Borsa Italiana. About 8 million passengers per year. B2B airport operator with high local visibility.

about: Israeli AI company based in Netanya whose system optimises airline pricing and revenue management in real time. Founded in 2019 by Roy Cohen and Uri Yerushalmi, its Large Market Model analyses demand and competitor fares to set prices and offers, with airlines such as Virgin Atlantic, WestJet and Azul reported as customers. Venture-funded with about $157 million. B2B aviation software, known in the airline industry.
cb_desc: Fetcherr uses Al to revolutionize airline revenue...

about: Minneapolis-based leisure and charter airline, listed on Nasdaq (SNCY), flying scheduled low-fare service from Minneapolis-St. Paul and charters and cargo for Amazon. Its Boeing 737 fleet flies to leisure destinations in the US, Mexico and the Caribbean, plus charter work for sports teams and the military. Agreed in early 2026 to be acquired by Allegiant. Consumer-facing airline with strong Minnesota recognition.

Jet Airways was an Indian full-service airline, based in Mumbai (the record shows Gurugram), which ceased operations in April 2019 under heavy debt. A consortium led by Jalan Kalrock won a revival bid in 2021, but the airline never restarted flying, and in 2024 the Supreme Court ordered its liquidation. Once a high-awareness consumer brand in India, but defunct, so not a sponsor candidate.

MNG Airlines is an Istanbul-based Turkish cargo airline, a division of the MNG Holding, founded in 1996, flying freighters and passenger charter flights from Istanbul and Ataturk airport to Europe, the Middle East, Asia and Africa. It also provides ground handling and logistics. Customers are freight forwarders and shippers. Crunchbase shows about 211 million dollars of funding. B2B airline, with low consumer awareness.

DFDS is a Copenhagen-based Danish shipping and logistics company, founded in 1866, operating ferries, passenger routes and freight services across Europe, including the North Sea, Baltic Sea, English Channel and Mediterranean, with trailer and logistics operations. It carries millions of passengers and has revenue near 24 billion Danish kroner. It is listed on Nasdaq Copenhagen (DFDS), with the Lauritzen Foundation as a major shareholder. A well-known ferry brand for European travelers.

Tunisair is the national flag-carrier airline of Tunisia, based in Tunis, operating scheduled and charter passenger and cargo flights to Europe, North Africa, the Middle East and West Africa from Tunis-Carthage, with a fleet of Airbus aircraft. Passengers are leisure, business and expatriate travellers. The Tunisian state is its main shareholder, and it is listed on the Bourse de Tunis (TAIR). Familiar national consumer brand in the Mediterranean region, with financial difficulties in recent years.

PLAY was an Icelandic low-cost airline based in Reykjavik, operating from Keflavik airport since 2021. It flew Airbus A320 and A321neo family aircraft on routes between Iceland, Europe and North America, selling point-to-point and connecting transatlantic tickets to leisure travellers, with ancillary fees. It was listed on Nasdaq First North Iceland under the ticker PLAY, and the Crunchbase figure shows about $145 million raised. The airline ceased operations in late September 2025 after failing to stabilise its finances. Known mostly to Icelandic and transatlantic budget travellers; no longer an active prospect.

Fly Leasing was an Irish aircraft leasing company based in Dun Laoghaire, Dublin, which owned a portfolio of around 100 narrowbody and widebody jets leased to airlines worldwide, earning rental income. It was listed on the NYSE through ADSs (FLY) until Carlyle Aviation Partners agreed to acquire it in 2021 for about $1.3 billion, including debt. B2B aviation finance business, with no consumer brand visibility.

Alliance Aviation Services is an Australian charter and wet-lease airline, based in Brisbane and listed on the ASX (AQZ), flying a fleet of Fokker and Embraer jets mainly for mining companies' fly-in fly-out workforces, and for airlines such as Qantas, Virgin Australia and Rex. It also maintains aircraft. Qantas moved to acquire the company from 2022. Sold mostly B2B, with little public consumer brand visibility, though its planes carry other airlines' livery.

Jeju Air is a South Korean low-cost airline based in Seoul (Jeju City), operating domestic and international routes within Asia to Japan, Southeast Asia, China and Guam, with a fleet of mostly Boeing 737-800s. Customers are leisure travellers. Founded in 2005 and listed on the KRX (089590), it is controlled by Aekyung Group. In December 2024 it suffered a fatal crash at Muan airport, leading to heavy scrutiny. Well-known regional consumer brand.

South African Airways is South Africa's state-owned flag carrier, based in Johannesburg and a member of Star Alliance. It was in business rescue from late 2019, then relaunched with a smaller operation in 2021, and the government sold a majority stake in 2025 to the Takatso consortium, though that deal was disputed. It flies domestic, regional and some long-haul routes with a modest fleet. Funding of about 3.5 billion rand is shown. National consumer brand, well known across Africa.

Frequent flyer programme of Avianca, the Colombian airline, operated as a separate business headquartered in Costa Rica that lets members earn miles from flights, credit cards, hotels and partners, and redeem them for flights on Avianca and Star Alliance airlines. It has millions of members across Latin America and sells miles to banks and retailers, from which it earns most of its revenue. It is owned by Advent International, separately from the airline. Large Latin American consumer loyalty brand.
